s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic symmetric hand swelling and erythema with intermittent exacerbations
salient_findings: 15-month history of swelling and redness of hands
Chronic joint pain in hands and back
Painless, symmetric swelling of both hands
Bilateral dorsal hand erythema and edema
Small-vessel ectasia and minimal perivascular lymphocytes on biopsy
key_facts: 35-year-old woman
Bipolar I disorder
Chronic joint pain
Occupational exposure to pool chemicals
No improvement with glove use
Prior treatments with topical mupirocin and emollients were unsuccessful
History of injecting heroin, buprenorphine, suboxone, and morphine
No tourniquet use during intravenous drug use
Intravenous drug use ceased three years prior to current symptoms
Symmetric swelling of both hands
Persistent hand and foot edema during pregnancy
Normal ejection fraction on echocardiogram
Negative antinuclear antibody, extractable nuclear antigen panel, and rheumatoid factor
Mildly elevated creatine kinase and aldolase
Normal creatinine levels, hepatic function tests, and hepatitis panels

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic Fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic symmetric hand swelling and erythema with intermittent exacerbations, history of intravenous drug use, and absence of typical autoimmune markers

shortlist.label: Scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic symmetric hand swelling and erythema, although lack of typical autoimmune markers and absence of skin thickening make it less likely

shortlist.label: Livedoid Vasculopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic symmetric hand swelling and erythema, with sharply demarcated borders and absence of typical autoimmune markers

shortlist.label: Chronic Venous Insufficiency
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic symmetric hand swelling and erythema, with history of intravenous drug use and possible venous damage

shortlist.label: Erythromelalgia
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic symmetric hand swelling and erythema, with intermittent exacerbations and absence of typical autoimmune markers

raw.rationale: The patient's history of symmetric swelling of both hands, chronic joint pain, and the presence of small-vessel ectasia and minimal perivascular lymphocytes on punch biopsy are consistent with Eosinophilic Fasciitis. The lack of improvement with topical treatments and the absence of other explanatory conditions also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Scleroderma
rejected.why: Negative antinuclear antibody and extractable nuclear antigen panel make this less likely

rejected.label: Livedoid Vasculopathy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not include the characteristic livedo reticularis or ulcerations

rejected.label: Chronic Venous Insufficiency
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms are not limited to one limb and do not include varicose veins or stasis dermatitis

rejected.label: Erythromelalgia
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not include the characteristic burning pain or warmth of the affected areas
